actions.action: Inspect plants, soil and nearby surfaces for adult gnats and check pots for excess moisture and organic debris
Place yellow sticky traps, cut into squares on skewers, in pots
Place raw potato chunks cut side down in the soil, then remove and replace infested ones every few days
Let the soil surface dry between waterings
Improve drainage by repotting in a mix with more perlite or sand
Clean up standing water and fix any plumbing or irrigation leaks
Buy and use only pasteurized potting mix, stored in a closed container
Solarize potting soil in a plastic bag in the sun for 4 to 6 weeks
Screen and caulk leaky windows and doors
Throw out the plant if it is severely infested
Apply a Bti product (e.g. Mosquito Bits, Gnatrol) as a soil drench, repeating about every five days
Mail-order Steinernema feltiae nematodes and apply as a soil drench
If Bti or nematodes are unavailable, take the plant outdoors, spray the soil surface and plant with a pyrethrin product, and bring it back after a day

verdict.reason: The answer is a generic fungus gnat page that mentions overwatering and root decay only as more common causes of wilting; its moisture-reduction and drainage advice partly matches the fix but omits chopping the rot, and nothing in it is likely to harm the plant.
